title: Fallback playback chronicle: AZ2->AZ1 routing oscillation
body:
Quick scratchpad / playback log — for personal triage. DO NOT PUBLISH verbatim.

Context:
- Incident observed 2026-03-09 15:08-15:40 UTC: customer traffic from eu-west (region routing policy) experienced repeated fallbacks from AZ2->AZ1 for ~32 minutes. User-facing error rate spiked to ~2.7% 503s for short windows.
- Affected service: smart-router (edge routing layer) routingPolicy=latency+preferred-az.
- Probable interaction: latency threshold + capacity-based fallback + stale route table entries.

Immediate reproduction steps I ran (local playback against staging routing endpoint):
1) Basic curl to debug endpoint to list region routes:
   curl -sS -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' \
     'https://staging-router.redwood.internal/v1/debug/routes?model=redwood-3b&region=eu-west' | jq -C .
   -> See route table: primary: az2.prod.pool.4 (score 0.72), fallback: az1.prod.pool.2 (score 0.67)

2) Triggered simulated request pattern (burst of 60 reqs/s) using siege:
   siege -c60 -t1M -b 'POST https://staging-router.redwood.internal/v1/generate' \
     'Authorization: Bearer TESTKEY' -H 'X-Region: eu-west' -H 'X-Client: playback'
   Observed: router logs show repeated 'invoking fallback' messages after 45s.

Commands I used to inspect infra (truncated outputs included):
- kubectl (router namespace)
  kubectl -n router get pods -l app=smart-router -o wide\  
  -> router-7d8f         Running   2/2     6d    10.0.32.14   az2-node-4
  -> router-6c3b         Running   2/2     4d    10.0.41.9    az1-node-2

- Checked router metrics (promql quick checks):
  requests_total{route="az2"} increased then dropped; 5xx_errors{route="az2"} spiked simultaneously.

- Example log snippet from router-7d8f (az2):
  [2026-03-09T15:09:12.435Z] INFO  route_eval.go:312 - request id=cli-89f2 route=az2 score=0.71 latency_est=120ms -> selected
  [2026-03-09T15:09:44.012Z] WARN  fallback_manager.go:88 - request id=cli-b4d1 fallback invoked from az2 -> az1 reason=capacity_exhausted threshold=0.75
  [2026-03-09T15:10:01.903Z] ERROR router.go:423 - request id=cli-c33a upstream error: 503 "no capacity"

- Router internal debug endpoint returned this when queried at 15:11UTC:
  {"route":"az2","last_health_check":"2026-03-09T15:10:55Z","recent_latency_p95_ms":186.3,"active_tokens":1420,"capacity_limit":1500}

Hypotheses (rank-ordered):
1) Short-lived capacity saturation on az2 pool: active_tokens approaching capacity_limit -> circuit triggers fallback. But why oscillation? Might be retry/backoff config too short causing churn.
2) Latency estimator overshoot: p95 jumps cause latency-first policy to move traffic and then quickly move back when p95 falls (thrash).
3) Stale capacity metadata: healthcheck cadence too low so decisions based on slightly stale snapshot (30s delay).
4) KV cache sync problem between router replicas (router-7d8f vs router-6c3b markets different view).

Things I tried and notes: 
- Increased healthcheck frequency in local staging (from 30s -> 10s) and replayed burst. Result: oscillation reduced but not eliminated. Suggests staleness is part of problem but not whole story.
- Hit /debug/state on both router pods and diffed the route tables; saw mismatch in 'last_seen_capacity_ts' (~12s difference).
- Turned on stricter backoff: retry_backoff_min 200ms -> 800ms. Replay: fewer rapid switches, but some fallbacks persisted (likely true capacity constraint).

Quick checks to run on production during next window (run from on-call jump box):
- curl -s 'https://router-prod.redwood.internal/v1/debug/pools?az=az2' | jq .
- kubectl -n router logs router-<pod> --since=60m | grep -E "fallback|capacity_exhausted|circuit" -n
- promql: increase(last_over_time(active_tokens[2m]), 5m) and check capacity utilization trends
- tcpdump on router host (rotate capture quickly) focusing on port to inference-backend to see connection resets

Repro recipe (staging) to approximate incident:
1) Deploy small change to staging routing policy: healthcheck_interval=10s, backoff_min=800ms (non-invasive, rollback-friendly).
2) Warm model pools by firing low-rate background pings for 5m.
3) Fire 60-80 rps ramp starting at t0 for 5m, observe router logs, prom, and backend pod metrics.
4) Correlate fallbacks with backend pod eviction/restarts or OOMs.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Are there background tasks evicting model workers in az2 around 15:00 UTC? Check k8s eviction events and node autoscaler logs.
- Confirm rate of config propagation for routing policies; is there a window where half the routers see one policy and half another? (config push timeline)
- Validate inference backend CPU/GPU throttling metrics around the spike.
- Add metric for per-route decision entropy (to quantify thrash).

Quick one-off mitigation (if we see this again prod):
- Increase fallback_hold_period to 30s (avoid immediate bounce back).
- Temporarily prefer capacity-weighted routing for eu-west until pool pressure subsides.
- Notify infra team to check node autoscaler and preemptible churn in az2.

Notes for postmortem (if confirmed):
- Timeline (UTC)
  15:07 - slight p95 uptick in az2 -> first micro-fallbacks
  15:09 - fallback rate grows, customer 5xxs appear
  15:17 - brief autoscaler activity observed (scale-up + scale-down?)
  15:40 - traffic normalizes after policy tweak and backoff tuning

Attached artifacts / quick links: JIRA-RT-4821 has playbook draft; infra PR #1228 contains an experiment to increase healthcheck cadence.

Final ad-hoc notes:
- If we add a long-lived 'sticky' decision window (e.g., 20s), we should measure latency percentiles impact before rolling to prod.
- Consider adding a rapid-sample path to read instantaneous pool saturation (not smoothed p95) to gate fallbacks during bursts.

-- end scratchpad --
